cm\nREWARD_ZONES = {\n    'A': (80, 130),\n    'B': (200, 250),\n    'C': (320, 370),\n}\nZONE_CENTERS = {k: (v[0] + v[1]) / 2 for k, v in REWARD_ZONES.items()}\nNEU_COEF = 0.7\nTAU = 0.7  # calcium indicator time constant for OASIS\nLICK_ERROR_THR = 0.35  # fraction of frames with cumsum lick > 2\nBASELINE_WINDOW = 300  # samples for maximin baseline (~20s at 15.5 Hz)\nDFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA = 2  # samples for Gaussian smoothing of dF/F\n\nDATA_DIR = '/app/data'\n\n# ============================================================\n# Utility functions\n# ============================================================\n\ndef nansmooth(a, sigma, axis=-1):\n    \"\"\"Gaussian smooth ignoring NaNs (from reference utilities.py).\"\"\"\n    nan_inds = np.isnan(a)\n    a_nanless = np.copy(a)\n    a_nanless[nan_inds] = 0\n    one = np.ones(a.shape)\n    one[nan_inds] = 0.001\n    a_nanless = gaussian_filter1d(a_nanless, sigma, axis=axis)\n    one = gaussian_filter1d(one, sigma, axis=axis)\n    return a_nanless / one\n\n\ndef compute_dff_and_deconvolve(F, Fneu, trial_starts, teleports, frame_rate, n_planes=1):\n    \"\"\"\n    Compute dF/F and deconvolved events following reference preprocessing.py.\n\n    Steps:\n    1. Extract F within trial boundaries, set rest to NaN\n    2. Neuropil subtraction: F -= NEU_COEF * Fneu\n    3. Add back neuropil mean per trial\n    4. Maximin baseline per trial\n    5. dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|\n    6. Smooth dF/F with 2-sample Gaussian\n    7. Deconvolve with OASIS\n\n    Args:\n        F: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) raw fluorescence\n        Fneu: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) neuropil fluorescence\n        trial_starts: array of trial start indices (1-indexed from NWB)\n        teleports: array of teleport indices (1-indexed from NWB)\n        frame_rate: imaging frame rate\n        n_planes: number of imaging planes\n\n    Returns:\n        events: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) deconvolved events\n        dff: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) dF/F\n    \"\"\"\n    # Transpose to (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for processing\n    F = F.T.astype(np.float64)\n    Fneu = Fneu.T.astype(np.float64)\n    n_neurons, n_timepoints = F.shape\n\n    # Step 1: Extract within trials only\n    f_ = np.full_like(F, np.nan)\n    f_neu_ = np.full_like(Fneu, np.nan)\n\n    start_inds = trial_starts.tolist()\n    stop_inds = teleports.tolist()\n\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        # Reference uses start-1:stop-1 (1-indexed to 0-indexed)\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        if s < 0:\n            s = 0\n        if e > n_timepoints:\n            e = n_timepoints\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]\n        f_neu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n\n    # Step 2: Neuropil subtraction\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * f_neu_\n\n    # Step 3-4: Baseline computation and dF/F per trial\n    nanmask = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    flow = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n    dff = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n    spks = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        if s < 0:\n            s = 0\n        if e > n_timepoints:\n            e = n_timepoints\n\n        # Add back neuropil mean per trial after subtraction\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(f_neu_[:, s:e], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n\n        # Maximin baseline: smooth, min filter, max filter\n        flow[:, s:e] = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], 15, axis=1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = minimum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = maximum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n\n    # dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|\n    dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n\n    # Step 6: Smooth dF/F with 2-sample Gaussian per trial\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        if s < 0:\n            s = 0\n        if e > n_timepoints:\n            e = n_timepoints\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n\n        # Step 7: Deconvolve with OASIS\n        trial_dff = dff[:, s:e].copy()\n        trial_dff[np.isnan(trial_dff)] = 0\n        spks[:, s:e] = oasis(trial_dff, 2000, TAU, frame_rate / n_planes)\n\n    return spks, dff\n\n\ndef determine_reward_zone_per_trial(position, rz_signal, trial_starts, teleports):\n    \"\"\"\n    Determine reward zone label (A, B, C) for each trial based on\n    where the reward_zone signal is nonzero.\n\n    Returns:\n        zone_labels: list of str ('A', 'B', 'C') per trial\n        zone_coords: list of (start, end) tuples per trial\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(trial_starts)\n    zone_labels = []\n    zone_coords = []\n\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_starts[i] - 1  # convert to 0-indexed\n        e = teleports[i] - 1\n\n        trial_pos = position[s:e]\n        trial_rz = rz_signal[s:e]\n\n        # Find positions where reward zone signal is nonzero\n        rz_active = trial_rz > 0\n        if np.any(rz_active):\n            rz_positions = trial_pos[rz_active]\n            rz_center = np.mean(rz_positions)\n        else:\n            # No reward zone signal - use previous trial's zone\n            if len(zone_labels) > 0:\n                zone_labels.append(zone_labels[-1])\n                zone_coords.append(zone_coords[-1])\n                continue\n            else:\n                # Default to zone A\n                zone_labels.append('A')\n                zone_coords.append(REWARD_ZONES['A'])\n                continue\n\n        # Classify zone by center position\n        dists = {k: abs(rz_center - c) for k, c in ZONE_CENTERS.items()}\n        zone = min(dists, key=dists.get)\n        zone_labels.append(zone)\n        zone_coords.append(REWARD_ZONES[zone])\n\n    return zone_labels, zone_coords\n\n\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position, zone_start, zone_end):\n    \"\"\"\n    Compute signed distance from position to reward zone.\n    Negative = before zone, 0 = in zone, positive = past zone.\n    \"\"\"\n    dist = np.zeros_like(position)\n    before = position < zone_start\n    inside = (position >= zone_start) & (position <= zone_end)\n    after = position > zone_end\n\n    dist[before] = position[before] - zone_start  # negative\n    dist[inside] = 0.0\n    dist[after] = position[after] - zone_end  # positive\n\n    return dist\n\n\ndef discretize_distance_to_rz(distance):\n    \"\"\"Discretize distance to reward zone into 7 bins per decoder spec.\"\"\"\n    bins = np.zeros(len(distance), dtype=np.int64)\n    bins[distance < -50] = 0\n    bins[(distance >= -50) & (distance < -10)] = 1\n    bins[(distance >= -10) & (distance < 0)] = 2\n    bins[distance == 0] = 3  # in zone\n    bins[(distance > 0) & (distance <= 10)] = 4\n    bins[(distance > 10) & (distance <= 50)] = 5\n    bins[distance > 50] = 6\n    return bins\n\n\ndef discretize_position(position):\n    \"\"\"Discretize position into 5 bins of 90cm each.\"\"\"\n    bins = np.zeros(len(position), dtype=np.int64)\n    bins[position < 90] = 0\n    bins[(position >= 90) & (position < 180)] = 1\n    bins[(position >= 180) & (position < 270)] = 2\n    bins[(position >= 270) & (position < 360)] = 3\n    bins[position >= 360] = 4\n    return bins\n\n\ndef discretize_speed(speed):\n    \"\"\"Discretize speed into 5 bins per decoder spec.\"\"\"\n    bins = np.zeros(len(speed), dtype=np.int64)\n    speed_abs = np.abs(speed)\n    bins[speed_abs < 2] = 0\n    bins[(speed_abs >= 2) & (speed_abs < 10)] = 1\n    bins[(speed_abs >= 10) & (speed_abs < 20)] = 2\n    bins[(speed_abs >= 20) & (speed_abs < 40)] = 3\n    bins[speed_abs >= 40] = 4\n    return bins\n\n\ndef determine_reward_per_trial(reward_timestamps, behav_timestamps, trial_starts, teleports):\n    \"\"\"\n    Determine if reward was delivered on each trial.\n    Uses the Reward timestamps to check if any reward event falls within trial.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(trial_starts)\n    rewarded = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\n\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_starts[i] - 1\n        e = teleports[i] - 1\n        t_start = behav_timestamps[s]\n        t_end = behav_timestamps[min(e, len(behav_timestamps) - 1)]\n\n        # Check if any reward timestamp falls within trial\n        in_trial = (reward_timestamps >= t_start) & (reward_timestamps <= t_end)\n        if np.any(in_trial):\n            rewarded[i] = 1\n\n    return rewarded\n\n\n# ============================================================\n# Main processing function\n# ============================================================\n\ndef process_session(nwb_path, show_processing=False, session_idx=0):\n    \"\"\"Process a single NWB file into decoder format.\"\"\"\n    t0 = time.time()\n\n    subject = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(nwb_path))\n    ses_id = os.path.basename(nwb_path).split('_')[1]\n    print(f\"  Processing {subject} {ses_id}...\")\n\n    with h5py.File(nwb_path, 'r') as f:\n        # ---- Load metadata ----\n        imaging_rate = f['acquisition/TwoPhotonSeries/imaging_plane/imaging_rate'][()]\n\n        # ---- Load behavioral data ----\n        bts = f['processing/behavior/BehavioralTimeSeries']\n        position = bts['position/data'][:]\n        speed = bts['speed/data'][:]\n        lick = bts['lick/data'][:]\n        trial_num = bts['trial number/data'][:]\n        trial_start_signal = bts['trial_start/data'][:]\n        teleport_signal = bts['teleport/data'][:]\n        environment = bts['environment/data'][:]\n        rz_signal = bts['reward_zone/data'][:]\n        behav_timestamps = bts['position/timestamps'][:]\n\n        # Reward events\n        reward_data = bts['Reward/data'][:]\n        reward_timestamps = bts['Reward/timestamps'][:]\n\n        # Autoreward\n        autoreward = bts['autoreward/data'][:]\n\n        # ---- Load neural data ----\n        ophys = f['processing/ophys']\n        iscell_full = ophys['ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/iscell'][:]\n        plane_idx = ophys['ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/planeIdx'][:]\n\n        # Get available planes\n        planes = sorted([k for k in ophys['Fluorescence'].keys() if k.startswith('plane')])\n\n        # Load and concatenate across planes\n        F_all = []\n        Fneu_all = []\n        cell_mask_all = []\n\n        for plane in planes:\n            F_plane = ophys[f'Fluorescence/{plane}/data'][:]\n            Fneu_plane = ophys[f'Neuropil/{plane}/data'][:]\n\n            # Get plane number\n            pnum = int(plane.replace('plane', ''))\n\n            # iscell for this plane's ROIs\n            plane_roi_mask = plane_idx == pnum\n            iscell_plane = iscell_full[plane_roi_mask, 0]\n\n            # Verify shape consistency\n            assert F_plane.shape[1] == np.sum(plane_roi_mask), \\\n                f\"Shape mismatch: F has {F_plane.shape[1]} cols but {np.sum(plane_roi_mask)} ROIs in plane {pnum}\"\n\n            F_all.append(F_plane)\n            Fneu_all.append(Fneu_plane)\n            cell_mask_all.append(iscell_plane > 0)\n\n        # Concatenate across planes\n        F_concat = np.concatenate(F_all, axis=1)\n        Fneu_concat = np.concatenate(Fneu_all, axis=1)\n        cell_mask = np.concatenate(cell_mask_all)\n\n        n_planes = len(planes)\n\n    # ---- Get trial indices ----\n    trial_start_inds = np.where(trial_start_signal > 0)[0] + 1  # convert to 1-indexed\n    teleport_inds = np.where(teleport_signal > 0)[0] + 1  # convert to 1-indexed\n\n    if len(trial_start_inds) != len(teleport_inds):\n        # Handle mismatch\n        min_len = min(len(trial_start_inds), len(teleport_inds))\n        trial_start_inds = trial_start_inds[:min_len]\n        teleport_inds = teleport_inds[:min_len]\n\n    n_trials = len(trial_start_inds)\n\n    # ---- Compute dF/F and deconvolved events ----\n    # Effective frame rate per plane\n    effective_rate = imaging_rate  # Already per-plane for multi-plane\n    if n_planes > 1:\n        # For multi-plane, imaging_rate is the combined rate\n        # Per-plane rate is imaging_rate / n_planes\n        effective_rate = imaging_rate / n_planes\n\n    t_dff = time.time()\n    events, dff = compute_dff_and_deconvolve(\n        F_concat, Fneu_concat, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds,\n        imaging_rate, n_planes\n    )\n    print(f\"    dF/F + deconv: {time.time() - t_dff:.1f}s\")\n\n    # Apply iscell filter\n    cell_indices = np.where(cell_mask)[0]\n    events_cells = events[cell_indices, :]  # (n_cells, n_timepoints)\n    n_neurons = len(cell_indices)\n\n    # ---- Determine reward zones ----\n    zone_labels, zone_coords = determine_reward_zone_per_trial(\n        position, rz_signal, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds\n    )\n\n    # ---- Determine reward per trial ----\n    rewarded = determine_reward_per_trial(\n        reward_timestamps, behav_timestamps, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds\n    )\n\n    # Also check autoreward\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n        e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n        if np.any(autoreward[s:e] > 0):\n            rewarded[i] = 1\n\n    # ---- Determine environment per trial ----\n    env_per_trial = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n        e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n        env_vals = environment[s:e]\n        valid_env = env_vals[env_vals >= 0]\n        if len(valid_env) > 0:\n            env_per_trial[i] = int(np.median(valid_env))\n        elif i > 0:\n            env_per_trial[i] = env_per_trial[i - 1]\n\n    # ---- Lick sensor error correction ----\n    lick_corrected = lick.copy()\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n        e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n        trial_lick = lick_corrected[s:e]\n        n_frames = len(trial_lick)\n        if n_frames > 0 and np.sum(trial_lick > 2) / n_frames > LICK_ERROR_THR:\n            lick_corrected[s:e] = 0\n\n    # Convert lick to binary\n    lick_binary = (lick_corrected > 0).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # ---- Build trial-level data ----\n    neural_trials = []\n    input_trials = []\n    output_trials = []\n\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1  # 0-indexed start\n        e = teleport_inds[i] - 1      # 0-indexed end\n\n        if e <= s:\n            continue\n\n        n_tp = e - s\n\n        # Neural: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n        trial_neural = events_cells[:, s:e].copy()\n        # Replace NaN with 0\n        trial_neural[np.isnan(trial_neural)] = 0\n        neural_trials.append(trial_neural.astype(np.float32))\n\n        # ---- Inputs ----\n        # Time from trial start (seconds)\n        time_from_start = np.arange(n_tp, dtype=np.float32) / effective_rate\n\n        # Per-trial inputs (broadcast to match time-varying shape)\n        env_type = np.float32(env_per_trial[i])\n        trial_number = np.float32(i)\n\n        # Previous trial outcome\n        if i == 0:\n            prev_outcome = np.float32(0)  # no previous trial\n        else:\n            prev_outcome = np.float32(rewarded[i - 1])\n\n        # input shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) for time-varying, (n_input,) for per-trial\n        # Mix of time-varying and per-trial\n        input_tv = time_from_start.reshape(1, -1)  # (1, n_tp)\n        input_pt = np.array([env_type, trial_number, prev_outcome], dtype=np.float32)  # (3,)\n\n        # Combine: first row is time-varying, rest are per-trial\n        # Per spec: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input,)\n        # We'll use a mixed approach: time-varying inputs get full shape, per-trial get scalar\n        inputs = np.vstack([\n            input_tv,  # (1, n_tp) - time from start\n            np.full((1, n_tp), env_type, dtype=np.float32),  # (1, n_tp) - env type\n            np.full((1, n_tp), trial_number, dtype=np.float32),  # (1, n_tp) - trial number\n            np.full((1, n_tp), prev_outcome, dtype=np.float32),  # (1, n_tp) - prev outcome\n        ]).astype(np.float32)\n        input_trials.append(inputs)\n\n        # ---- Outputs ----\n        trial_pos = position[s:e]\n        trial_speed = speed[s:e]\n        trial_lick = lick_binary[s:e]\n\n        # Distance to reward zone\n        zs, ze = zone_coords[i]\n        dist = compute_distance_to_reward_zone(trial_pos, zs, ze)\n        dist_binned = discretize_distance_to_rz(dist)\n\n        # Absolute position\n        pos_binned = discretize_position(trial_pos)\n\n        # Speed\n        speed_binned = discretize_speed(trial_speed)\n\n        # Per-trial outputs\n        zone_label = zone_labels[i]\n        rz_loc = {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}[zone_label]\n        reward_out = int(rewarded[i])\n\n        outputs = np.vstack([\n            dist_binned.reshape(1, -1),    # (1, n_tp) - distance to RZ\n            pos_binned.reshape(1, -1),      # (1, n_tp) - absolute position\n            speed_binned.reshape(1, -1),    # (1, n_tp) - speed\n            trial_lick.reshape(1, -1),      # (1, n_tp) - lick\n            np.full((1, n_tp), rz_loc, dtype=np.int64),      # (1, n_tp) - RZ location\n            np.full((1, n_tp), reward_out, dtype=np.int64),   # (1, n_tp) - reward outcome\n        ]).astype(np.int64)\n        output_trials.append(outputs)\n\n    elapsed = time.time() - t0\n    print(f\"    {subject} {ses_id}: {n_neurons} neurons, {len(neural_trials)} trials, {elapsed:.1f}s\")\n\n    # ---- Processing visualization ----\n    if show_processing and session_idx < 2:\n        plot_processing(\n            subject, ses_id, position, speed, lick_binary,\n            events_cells, dff[cell_indices, :], trial_start_inds, teleport_inds,\n            zone_labels, zone_coords, rewarded, effective_rate,\n            neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials\n        )\n\n    session_info = {\n        'subject': subject.replace('sub-', ''),\n        'session': ses_id,\n        'n_neurons': n_neurons,\n        'n_trials': len(neural_trials),\n        'imaging_rate': effective_rate,\n        'zone_labels': zone_labels,\n        'rewarded': rewarded,\n        'env': env_per_trial,\n    }\n\n    return neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials, session_info\n\n\ndef plot_processing(subject, ses_id, position, speed, lick, events, dff,\n                    trial_starts, teleports, zone_labels, zone_coords,\n                    rewarded, frame_rate, neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials):\n    \"\"\"Plot processing visualizations for sanity checking.\"\"\"\n    import matplotlib\n    matplotlib.use('Agg')\n    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(6, 2, figsize=(20, 24))\n    fig.suptitle(f'{subject} {ses_id}', fontsize=16)\n\n    # Plot 1: Raw position and reward zone across trials\n    ax = axes[0, 0]\n    for i in range(min(len(trial_starts), 10)):\n        s = trial_starts[i] - 1\n        e = teleports[i] - 1\n        t = np.arange(s, e) / frame_rate\n        ax.plot(t, position[s:e], alpha=0.5)\n        zs, ze = zone_coords[i]\n        ax.axhspan(zs, ze, alpha=0.1, color='green')\n    ax.set_title('Position (first 10 trials)')\n    ax.set_ylabel('Position (cm)')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\n\n    # Plot 2: Neural activity example (first 3 cells)\n    ax = axes[0, 1]\n    n_cells_plot = min(3, events.shape[0])\n    for c in range(n_cells_plot):\n        s = trial_starts[0] - 1\n        e = teleports[0] - 1\n        t = np.arange(s, e) / frame_rate\n        trace = events[c, s:e]\n        trace[np.isnan(trace)] = 0\n        ax.plot(t, trace + c * np.nanmax(trace) * 1.5, alpha=0.7)\n    ax.set_title('Deconvolved events (trial 0, first 3 cells)')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\n\n    # Plot 3: dF/F example\n    ax = axes[1, 0]\n    for c in range(n_cells_plot):\n        s = trial_starts[0] - 1\n        e = teleports[0] - 1\n        t = np.arange(s, e) / frame_rate\n        trace = dff[c, s:e]\n        trace[np.isnan(trace)] = 0\n        ax.plot(t, trace + c * 2, alpha=0.7)\n    ax.set_title('dF/F (trial 0, first 3 cells)')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\n\n    # Plot 4: Speed distribution\n    ax = axes[1, 1]\n    valid_speed = speed[speed > -100]\n    ax.hist(valid_speed, bins=50, alpha=0.7)\n    ax.axvline(2, color='r', linestyle='--', label='2 cm/s threshold')\n    ax.set_title('Speed distribution')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Speed (cm/s)')\n    ax.legend()\n\n    # Plot 5: Output discretization - distance to RZ\n    ax = axes[2, 0]\n    trial_idx = 5\n    if trial_idx < len(output_trials):\n        out = output_trials[trial_idx]\n        t = np.arange(out.shape[1]) / frame_rate\n        ax.plot(t, out[0, :], '.', markersize=2)\n        ax.set_title(f'Distance to RZ (trial {trial_idx})')\n        ax.set_ylabel('Bin')\n        ax.set_yticks(range(7))\n\n    # Plot 6: Output discretization - position\n    ax = axes[2, 1]\n    if trial_idx < len(output_trials):\n        ax.plot(t, out[1, :], '.', markersize=2)\n        ax.set_title(f'Absolute position (trial {trial_idx})')\n        ax.set_ylabel('Bin')\n        ax.set_yticks(range(5))\n\n    # Plot 7: Output - speed\n    ax = axes[3, 0]\n    if trial_idx < len(output_trials):\n        ax.plot(t, out[2, :], '.', markersize=2)\n        ax.set_title(f'Speed (trial {trial_idx})')\n        ax.set_ylabel('Bin')\n        ax.set_yticks(range(5))\n\n    # Plot 8: Output - lick\n    ax = axes[3, 1]\n    if trial_idx < len(output_trials):\n        ax.plot(t, out[3, :], '.', markersize=2)\n        ax.set_title(f'Lick (trial {trial_idx})')\n        ax.set_ylabel('0/1')\n\n    # Plot 9: Reward zone per trial\n    ax = axes[4, 0]\n    zone_numeric = [{'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}[z] for z in zone_labels]\n    ax.plot(zone_numeric, 'o-', markersize=3)\n    ax.set_title('Reward zone per trial')\n    ax.set_ylabel('Zone (A=0, B=1, C=2)')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Trial')\n    ax.set_yticks([0, 1, 2])\n    ax.set_yticklabels(['A', 'B', 'C'])\n\n    # Plot 10: Reward outcome per trial\n    ax = axes[4, 1]\n    ax.plot(rewarded, 'o', markersize=3)\n    reward_rate = np.mean(rewarded)\n    ax.set_title(f'Reward outcome (rate={reward_rate:.2f})')\n    ax.set_ylabel('Rewarded')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Trial')\n\n    # Plot 11: Input time from start\n    ax = axes[5, 0]\n    if trial_idx < len(input_trials):\n        inp = input_trials[trial_idx]\n        t = np.arange(inp.shape[1]) / frame_rate\n        ax.plot(t, inp[0, :])\n        ax.set_title(f'Input: time from trial start (trial {trial_idx})')\n        ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\n\n    # trial_start_idx) / imaging_rate | Continuous, time-varying |\n   181→| NWB environment | `input[1]`: environment_type | 0=ENV1, 1=ENV2 | Binary, per-trial |\n   182→| NWB trial number | `input[2]`: trial_number | 0-indexed trial number | Continuous, per-trial |\n   183→| Previous trial reward | `input[3]`: previous_trial_outcome | 0=omitted, 1=rewarded | Binary, per-trial |\n   184→| Position vs reward zone | `output[0]`: distance_to_reward_zone | Discretize signed distance to nearest rz boundary into 7 bins | Time-varying |\n   185→| NWB position | `output[1]`: absolute_position | Discretize into 5 bins of 90cm each | Time-varying |\n   186→| NWB speed | `output[2]`: speed | Discretize into 5 bins | Time-varying |\n   187→| NWB lick | `output[3]`: lick | Binary (any lick > 0) | Time-varying |\n   188→| Reward zone identity | `output[4]`: reward_zone_location | 0=A, 1=B, 2=C based on zone position | Per-trial |\n   189→| Reward delivery | `output[5]`: reward_outcome | 0=no, 1=yes | Per-trial |\n   190→\n   191→### Key Decisions\n   192→\n   193→1. **Recompute dF/F from F and Fneu**: The NWB Deconvolved data is suite2p's raw deconvolution, not the custom dF/F + OASIS used in the paper. Must recompute to match reference processing.\n   194→\n   195→2. **No speed threshold filtering**: The reference applies speed > 2 cm/s filter, but our decoder outputs include speed with a < 2 cm/s bin. Removing low-speed timepoints would make speed bin 0 empty. This difference from the reference is justified by the decoder specification.\n   196→\n   197→3. **Include ALL cells passing iscell**: The reference decoder uses cell-type subpopulations (RR, TR), but our decoder uses all cells. We apply iscell filter only (manual curation). We do NOT apply the interneuron correlation filter because: (a) it would require computing the full dF/F timeseries first and correlating with speed, (b) it only excludes ~0.42% of cells, (c) the iscell manual curation already removed obvious interneurons.\n   198→\n   199→4. **Time bin = imaging frame**: Each time bin is one imaging frame (~64.5 ms at 15.5 Hz). This matches the reference temporal resolution.\n   200→\n   201→5. **Trial definition**: Each trial runs from trial_start to teleport. Teleport/ITI periods excluded (set to NaN in reference).\n   202→\n   203→6. **Multi-plane animals (m17, m18)**: Pool neurons from both planes (matching reference). Neural data from plane0 and plane1 concatenated.\n   204→\n   205→7. **Distance to reward zone**: Compute as signed distance from position to nearest point in the reward zone [start, end]. Negative = before zone, 0 = in zone, positive = past zone. Discretize per decoder spec.\n   206→\n   207→8. **Reward zone determination per trial**: Determine from position where reward_zone signal > 0. Zone A: center ~105 cm, Zone B: center ~225 cm, Zone C: center ~345 cm.\n   208→\n   209→9. **Reward outcome per trial**: Determined from Reward timestamps array - check if any reward event falls within trial boundaries.\n   210→\n   211→10. **Lick sensor error correction**: Following reference, if >35% of frames in a trial have cumulative lick count > 2, set lick to 0 for that trial (matching reference behavior.py).\n   212→\n   213→### Planned Sanity Checks\n   214→- [ ] Total session count matches 152\n   215→- [ ] Neuron counts per session match range 155-2172 (after curation)\n   216→- [ ] Trial counts per session match data\n   217→- [ ] Reward omission rate ~15%\n   218→- [ ] Reward zone positions match A/B/C definitions\n   219→- [ ] Position range 0-450 cm within trials\n   220→- [ ] Speed distribution reasonable\n   221→- [ ] dF/F computation produces reasonable traces\n   222→\n   223→---\n   224→\n   225→## Step 6: Script Development\n   226→**Status**: COMPLETE\n   227→\n   228→- Full conversion script written: `/app/convert_data.py`\n   229→- Implements custom dF/F pipeline (neuropil subtraction, maximin baseline, Gaussian smooth, OASIS deconvolution)\n   230→- Supports `--sample`, `--full`, and `--show-processing` flags\n   231→- Handles multi-plane animals (m17, m18)\n   232→- All decoder inputs/outputs implemented per specification\n   233→\n   234→---\n   235→\n   236→## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\n   237→**Status**: COMPLETE\n   238→\n   239→- Sample data (2 sessions: m11/ses-03, m12/ses-03) converted successfully\n   240→- Data format verified with `train_decoder.py --verify-only` - \"A flexible hippocampal population code for experience relative to reward\"\n- **Date started**: 2026-09-21\n- **Goal**: Convert 2P calcium imaging data from NWB to decoder-compatible format\n- **Data source**: DANDI:001361 (NWB files with behavior + ophys)\n\n## Step 0: Setup and Initialization\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nDirectory contents:\n- `code/` - Reference code repository (Sosa_et_al_2024)\n- `data/` - NWB data files organized by subject (sub-m3, sub-m4, sub-m7, sub-m11..m15, sub-m17..m19)\n- `paper.pdf` - Reference paper\n- `methods.txt` - Extracted methods text\n- `decoder.py` - Decoder model code\n- `train_decoder.py` - Decoder training script\n\nPython environment: numpy 2.4.4, torch 2.6.0+cu124, GPU available\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `dff()` | preprocessing.py | PROCESSING | Compute dF/F with maximin baseline, optionally deconvolve with OASIS |\n| `get_timeseries_data()` | glmUtils.py | LOADING | Extract behavioral + neural timeseries per session |\n| `get_trial_types()` | behavior.py | LOADING | Get isreward, morph per trial |\n| `get_reward_zones()` | behavior.py | LOADING | Get reward zone coordinates per trial from scene name |\n| `define_trial_subsets()` | behavior.py | LOADING | Split trials into pre/post switch sets |\n| `multi_anim_sess()` | utilities.py | PROCESSING | Process all animals for one day: compute dF/F, place cells |\n| `CircularRegression` | decode.py | PROCESSING | Circular linear decoder for position |\n| `train_vs_test_blocks()` | decode.py | PROCESSING | Cross-validated decoder training |\n| `correct_lick_sensor_error()` | behavior.py | CURATION | Remove trials with stuck lick sensor (>35% threshold) |\n\n### Notes\n- The reference decoder predicts **circular reward-relative position** using a circular-linear regression, NOT the multi-output categorical decoder we are training\n- Neural data used: `sess.timeseries['events']` = custom dF/F -> OASIS deconvolved events\n- Speed threshold of 2 cm/s applied in `get_timeseries_data()` to mask out low-speed timepoints\n- Lick sensor error: trials where >35% of frames have cumulative lick > 2 are set to NaN\n- The reference decoder uses cell-type subpopulations (RR, TR, nonreward_remap), but we use ALL cells\n- Reward zone locations: A=[80,130], B=[200,250], C=[320,370] (from `reward_zone_dict` using X, Y, Z keys)\n\n### dF/F Processing Pipeline (from preprocessing.py)\n1. Extract F within trial boundaries (trial_start to teleport), set rest to NaN\n2. Neuropil subtraction: F -= 0.7 * Fneu (for single-channel)\n3. For dual-channel (m17, m18): additional bleedthrough correction\n4. Add back neuropil mean per trial after subtraction\n5. Maximin baseline: smooth F with [0,15] Gaussian, then min filter (300 samples), then max filter (300 samples)\n6. dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|\n7. Smooth dF/F with 2-sample Gaussian\n8. Deconvolve with OASIS: `dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau=0.7, frame_rate/n_planes)`\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n- 11 subjects: m3, m4, m7, m11, m12, m13, m14, m15, m17, m18, m19\n- Each subject has 12-14 NWB files (sessions), one per day\n- m11 starts at ses-03 (imaging began day 3), all others start at ses-01\n- NWB files contain:\n  - `processing/ophys/Fluorescence/plane{N}/data`: raw fluorescence (timepoints x ROIs)\n  - `processing/ophys/Neuropil/plane{N}/data`: neuropil fluorescence\n  - `processing/ophys/Deconvolved/plane{N}/data`: suite2p deconvolution (NOT custom)\n  - `processing/ophys/ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/iscell`: (n_rois, 2) cell classification\n  - `processing/ophys/ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/planeIdx`: plane assignment per ROI\n  - `processing/behavior/BehavioralTimeSeries/`: position, speed, lick, trial_start, teleport, trial number, environment, reward_zone, Reward, autoreward, scanning\n- Multi-plane animals (m17, m18): have plane0 and plane1 in Fluorescence/Deconvolved groups\n  - Imaging rate ~31 Hz interleaved -> ~15.5 Hz per plane\n  - Paper says \"planes were pooled for all analyses\"\n\n### Dataset Size (from data files)\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Neurons (total, iscell) | 138,678 |\n| Neurons / session (mean) | 912.4 |\n| Subjects | 11 |\n| Sessions / subject | 12-14 (152 total) |\n| Trials (total) | 12,217 |\n| Trials / session (mean) | 80.4, range 41-100 |\n| Imaging rate | ~15.5 Hz (single plane) |\n| Track length | 450 cm |\n\n### Key Behavioral Variables in NWB\n- `position`: 0-450 cm on track, -500 in teleport zone, negative before track start\n- `speed`: cm/s, includes negative values\n- `lick`: cumulative lick count per frame (0-6)\n- `trial number`: -1 outside trials, 0-indexed within session\n- `trial_start`: binary event (1 at trial start)\n- `teleport`: binary event (1 at teleport)\n- `environment`: -1 before scanning, 0=ENV1, 1=ENV2\n- `reward_zone`: 0-6, encodes reward zone state\n- `Reward`: separate array with reward event timestamps (sparse)\n- `autoreward`: binary, marks auto-reward delivery\n\n---\n\n## Step 3: Reference Text Reading\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Expected Statistics (from paper/methods)\n| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |\n|-----------|-------|--------------|\n| Neurons / session | 155-2172 | \"155-2,172 putative pyramidal neurons per session\" |\n| Subjects (switch task) | 11 | \"n = 11 mice\" (switch task) |\n| 0.85% | \"Pearson correlation >0.5 with speed\" |\n\n### Processing Details\n- Temporal alignment: All data aligned to 2P imaging frames (~15.5 Hz)\n- dF/F computed per trial with maximin baseline (20s sliding window)\n- Deconvolved with OASIS (suite2p implementation)\n- Activity outside trial periods set to NaN (teleport periods excluded for most sessions)\n- Auto-reward on first 10 trials of new condition\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules**:\n1. Suite2p manual curation: iscell flag (removes multi-soma ROIs, dendrites, non-responsive, overexpressing, putative interneurons)\n2. Speed-correlated interneuron exclusion: Pearson r > 0.5 between dF/F and running speed (~0.42% excluded)\n\n**Trial curation rules**:\n1. Lick sensor error: trials with >35% of frames having cumulative lick > 2 -> lick data set to NaN for that trial\n2. All valid trials (trial_number >= 0) included\n\n### Decoders Trained in Paper\n| Decoded variable | Method | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Circular reward-relative position | Circular-linear regression | cos(y - y_hat) score, ~0.1-0.6 for RR cells |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Paper says | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| NWB Deconvolved | Raw suite2p deconv (no NaN in ITI) | Values 0-2484, no NaN | Custom dF/F + OASIS | Must recompute dF/F from F and Fneu |\n| Neurons/session | iscell filter | 155-2281 per session | 155-2172 | Close match; slight difference may be from interneuron exclusion |\n| m18 iscell count | 2281 in iscell but only 1994 in plane0 data | Multi-plane: iscell=4857 total, 2281 cells | Planes pooled | iscell covers both planes; need to use planeIdx to map |\n| Trials per session | Some sessions have fewer: m4-ses-04=41, m4-ses-09=50, m13-ses-13=60 | 41-100 | 80.5 +/- 7.4 | Some sessions ended early; include all |\n| Environment encoding | env=0 or env=1 in NWB | -1 before scanning | ENV1=0, ENV2=1 | Use env value per trial (ignoring -1) |\n\n### Key Consistency Check\n- Paper says 11 switch mice, data has 11 subjects -> consistent\n- Paper says ~80 trials/session, data shows mean 80.4 -> consistent\n- Paper says 155-2172 neurons/session, data shows 155-2281 (before interneuron filter) -> consistent\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Variable Mapping\n\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|-------|\n| Custom dF/F + OASIS deconv of F, Fneu | `neural` | Compute dF/F with maximin baseline, deconvolve, filter by iscell | Shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) per trial |\n| Timestamps within trial | `input[0]`: time_from_trial_start | (frame_idx - trial_start_idx) / imaging_rate | Continuous, time-varying |\n| NWB environment | `input[1]`: environment_type | 0=ENV1, 1=ENV2 | Binary, per-trial |\n| NWB trial number | `input[2]`: trial_number | 0-indexed trial number | Continuous, per-trial |\n| Previous trial reward | `input[3]`: previous_trial_outcome | 0=omitted, 1=rewarded | Binary, per-trial |\n| Position vs reward zone | `output[0]`: distance_to_reward_zone | Discretize signed distance to nearest rz boundary into 7 bins | Time-varying |\n| NWB position | `output[1]`: absolute_position | Discretize into 5 bins of 90cm each | Time-varying |\n| NWB speed | `output[2]`: speed | Discretize into 5 bins | Time-varying |\n| NWB lick | `output[3]`: lick | Binary (any lick > 0) | Time-varying |\n| Reward zone identity | `output[4]`: reward_zone_location | 0=A, 1=B, 2=C based on zone position | Per-trial |\n| Reward delivery | `output[5]`: reward_outcome | 0=no, 1=yes | Per-trial |\n\n### Key Decisions\n\n1. **Recompute dF/F from F and Fneu**: The NWB Deconvolved data is suite2p's raw deconvolution, not the custom dF/F + OASIS used in the paper. Must recompute to match reference processing.\n\n2. **No speed threshold filtering**: The reference applies speed > 2 cm/s filter, but our decoder outputs include speed with a < 2 cm/s bin. Removing low-speed timepoints would make speed bin 0 empty. This difference from the reference is justified by the decoder specification.\n\n3. **Include ALL cells passing iscell**: The reference decoder uses cell-type subpopulations (RR, TR), but our decoder uses all cells. We apply iscell filter only (manual curation). We do NOT apply the interneuron correlation filter because: (a) it would require computing the full dF/F timeseries first and correlating with speed, (b) it only excludes ~0.42% of cells, (c) the iscell manual curation already removed obvious interneurons.\n\n4. **Time bin = imaging frame**: Each time bin is one imaging frame (~64.5 ms at 15.5 Hz). This matches the reference temporal resolution.\n\n5. **Trial definition**: Each trial runs from trial_start to teleport. Teleport/ITI periods excluded (set to NaN in reference).\n\n6. **Multi-plane animals (m17, m18)**: Pool neurons from both planes (matching reference). Neural data from plane0 and plane1 concatenated.\n\n7. **Distance to reward zone**: Compute as signed distance from position to nearest point in the reward zone [start, end]. Negative = before zone, 0 = in zone, positive = past zone. Discretize per decoder spec.\n\n8. **Reward zone determination per trial**: Determine from position where reward_zone signal > 0. Zone A: center ~105 cm, Zone B: center ~225 cm, Zone C: center ~345 cm.\n\n9. **Reward outcome per trial**: Determined from Reward timestamps array - check if any reward event falls within trial boundaries.\n\n10. **Lick sensor error correction**: Following reference, if >35% of frames in a trial have cumulative lick count > 2, set lick to 0 for that trial (matching reference behavior.py).\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] Total session count matches 152\n- [ ] Neuron counts per session match range 155-2172 (after curation)\n- [ ] Trial counts per session match data\n- [ ] Reward omission rate ~15%\n- [ ] Reward zone positions match A/B/C definitions\n- [ ] Position range 0-450 cm within trials\n- [ ] Speed distribution reasonable\n- [ ] dF/F computation produces reasonable traces\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n- Full conversion script written: `/app/convert_data.py`\n- Implements custom dF/F pipeline (neuropil subtraction, maximin baseline, Gaussian smooth, OASIS deconvolution)\n- Supports `--sample`, `--full`, and `--show-processing` flags\n- Handles multi-plane animals (m17, m18)\n- All decoder inputs/outputs implemented per specification\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n- Sample data (2 sessions: m11/ses-03, m12/ses-03) converted successfully\n- Data format verified with `train_decoder.py --verify-only` - Good spatial information encoded in CA1. The 7-bin discretization is fairly fine-grained; accuracy is consistent with known place cell properties.\n\n2. **absolute_position (0.65)**: 3.2x chance. Strongest spatial output. Expected - hippocampal place cells encode absolute position strongly.\n\n3. **speed (0.59)**: 3.0x chance. Speed is known to modulate hippocampal firing rates. Good decoding performance.\n\n4. **lick (0.75)**: 1.5x chance. Binary output makes this easier. Licking is anticipatory near reward zones, so neural correlates are expected.\n\n5. **reward_zone_location (0.84)**: 2.5x chance. Highest accuracy. This makes sense - after ~30 trials in each zone, the population builds strong zone-specific representations. This is consistent with the paper's finding that reward-relative cells remap to new reward locations.\n\n6. **reward_outcome (0.58)**: 1.2x chance. Weakest output but still above chance. Reward outcome is only determined at end of trial but the label is applied to all timepoints, making this harder to decode from moment-to-moment neural activity. The 85% reward rate also means the class imbalance makes balanced accuracy harder.\n\n### Potential Improvements (not implemented)\n- Per-session decoding rather than pooled across sessions (different cell populations)\n- Speed threshold filtering (but would lose speed bin 0)\n- Interneuron exclusion (minimal impact, ~0.42%)\n- More sophisticated architectures (RNN, attention)\n\n### No Issues Found\n- Data format passes all validation checks\n- All outputs above chance\n- Consistent with known hippocampal physiology\n- No obvious errors in processing pipeline\n\n---\n\n## Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n- README.md created with dataset overview, quick start, data format, and decoder results\n- All output files verified present\n- CONVERSION_NOTES.md updated through all steps\n","numLines":366,"startLine":1,"totalLines":366}}}

How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu following the paper's pipeline: (1) extract F within trial boundaries (set rest to NaN), (2) subtract 0.7 * Fneu, (3) add back neuropil mean per trial, (4) maximin baseline (Gaussian smooth sigma=15, min filter 300 samples, max filter 300 samples), (5) dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|, (6) smooth with 2-sample Gaussian, (7) deconvolve with OASIS (tau=0.7, frame_rate/n_planes). Cells from multiple planes are concatenated. The AI does NOT use the `keep_teleports` metadata from `teleport_metadata.py` -- it always restricts the baseline to within-trial windows.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_dff_and_deconvolve(F, Fneu, trial_starts, teleports, frame_rate, n_planes=1):\n    ...\n    start_inds = trial_starts.tolist()\n    stop_inds = teleports.tolist()\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]\n        f_neu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * f_neu_\n    ...\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        ...\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(f_neu_[:, s:e], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        flow[:, s:e] = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], 15, axis=1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = minimum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = maximum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n    dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n    ...\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n        ...\n        spks[:, s:e] = oasis(trial_dff, 2000, TAU, frame_rate / n_planes)\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES describe the dF/F pipeline accurately. The omission of `keep_teleports` is not documented as a deliberate decision; the CONVERSION_NOTES mention \"Activity outside trial periods set to NaN (teleport periods excluded for most sessions)\" but do not discuss that some sessions should include teleport periods in the baseline window.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only the `iscell` filter is applied (suite2p manual curation). The AI explicitly decides NOT to apply the putative interneuron filter (dF/F correlated with speed at r > 0.5). The iscell filter is applied AFTER computing dF/F (i.e., dF/F is computed for all ROIs, then subsetted).\n\nii.\n```python\niscell_full = ophys['ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/iscell'][:]\n...\ncell_mask_all.append(iscell_plane > 0)\n...\nevents, dff = compute_dff_and_deconvolve(F_concat, Fneu_concat, ...)  # all ROIs\ncell_indices = np.where(cell_mask)[0]\nevents_cells = events[cell_indices, :]  # filter after\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES state: \"We do NOT apply the interneuron correlation filter because: (a) it would require computing the full dF/F timeseries first and correlating with speed, (b) it only excludes ~0.42% of cells, (c) the iscell manual curation already removed obvious interneurons.\"\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Neural data is aligned to trial start. The trial boundaries (from `trial_start` to `teleport`) define the slice of neural data for each trial, so alignment is inherent in the slicing.\n\nii.\n```python\ns = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\ne = teleport_inds[i] - 1\ntrial_neural = events_cells[:, s:e].copy()\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify alignment to start of trial. No additional temporal shifting is needed.\n\n## 2-e. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. The data is kept at the original imaging frame rate (~15.5 Hz, ~64.5 ms per frame). No rebinning is applied. The time bin size is computed as `1000 / 15.5078125` ms.\n\nii.\n```python\n'time_bin_size': 1000.0 / 15.5078125,  # ms per frame\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES confirm \"Time bin = imaging frame: Each time bin is one imaging frame (~64.5 ms at 15.5 Hz).\"\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Time from start of trial in seconds* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the frame index within the trial and the effective imaging rate. NOT from the stored behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\ntime_from_start = np.arange(n_tp, dtype=np.float32) / effective_rate\n```\n\niii. The AI handles missing reward zone data by using the previous trial's zone.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. Signed distance from animal's position to the nearest edge of the assigned reward zone. Negative = before zone, 0 = in zone, positive = past zone. Then discretized into 7 bins.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position, zone_start, zone_end):\n    dist = np.zeros_like(position)\n    before = position < zone_start\n    inside = (position >= zone_start) & (position <= zone_end)\n    after = position > zone_end\n    dist[before] = position[before] - zone_start\n    dist[inside] = 0.0\n    dist[after] = position[after] - zone_end\n    return dist\n```\n\niii. Standard signed distance computation. Matches the reference logic.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Discretized into 7 bins using explicit boolean conditions:\n- 0: < -50 cm\n- 1: -50 to -10 cm\n- 2: -10 to 0 cm\n- 3: == 0 cm (in zone)\n- 4: >0 to 10 cm\n- 5: 10 to 50 cm\n- 6: > 50 cm\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_distance_to_rz(distance):\n    bins = np.zeros(len(distance), dtype=np.int64)\n    bins[distance < -50] = 0\n    bins[(distance >= -50) & (distance < -10)] = 1\n    bins[(distance >= -10) & (distance < 0)] = 2\n    bins[distance == 0] = 3\n    bins[(distance > 0) & (distance <= 10)] = 4\n    bins[(distance > 10) & (distance <= 50)] = 5\n    bins[distance > 50] = 6\n    return bins\n```\n\niii. The bins match the instructions. The reference uses `np.digitize` with a `1e-6` separator between \"0 cm\" and \">0 cm\" bins, while the AI uses explicit `== 0` and `> 0` conditions. The CONVERSION_NOTES do not discuss a minimum trial length threshold. The reference code filters trials with fewer than 50 timepoints.\n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. Neural data is derived from the raw Fluorescence (F) and Neuropil (Fneu) traces stored in the NWB file under `processing/ophys/Fluorescence/plane{N}/data` and `processing/ophys/Neuropil/plane{N}/data`. The NWB `Deconvolved` field is NOT used.\n\nii.\n```python\nophys = f['processing/ophys']\n...\nfor plane in planes:\n    F_plane = ophys[f'Fluorescence/{plane}/data'][:]\n    Fneu_plane = ophys[f'Neuropil/{plane}/data'][:]\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES correctly identify that the NWB Deconvolved data is suite2p's raw deconvolution, not the paper's custom dF/F + OASIS pipeline. The AI decided to recompute from F and Fneu.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu following the paper's pipeline: (1) extract F within trial boundaries (set rest to NaN), (2) subtract 0.7 * Fneu, (3) add back neuropil mean per trial, (4) maximin baseline (Gaussian smooth sigma=15, min filter 300 samples, max filter 300 samples), (5) dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|, (6) smooth with 2-sample Gaussian, (7) deconvolve with OASIS (tau=0.7, frame_rate/n_planes). Cells from multiple planes are concatenated. The AI does NOT use the `keep_teleports` metadata from `teleport_metadata.py` -- it always restricts the baseline to within-trial windows.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_dff_and_deconvolve(F, Fneu, trial_starts, teleports, frame_rate, n_planes=1):\n    ...\n    start_inds = trial_starts.tolist()\n    stop_inds = teleports.tolist()\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]\n        f_neu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * f_neu_\n    ...\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        ...\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(f_neu_[:, s:e], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        flow[:, s:e] = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], 15, axis=1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = minimum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = maximum_filter1d(flow[:, s:e], BASELINE_WINDOW, axis=-1)\n    dff[:, nanmask] = (f_[:, nanmask] - flow[:, nanmask]) / np.abs(flow[:, nanmask])\n    ...\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n        ...\n        spks[:, s:e] = oasis(trial_dff, 2000, TAU, frame_rate / n_planes)\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES describe the dF/F pipeline accurately. The omission of `keep_teleports` is not documented as a deliberate decision; the CONVERSION_NOTES mention \"Activity outside trial periods set to NaN (teleport periods excluded for most sessions)\" but do not discuss that some sessions should include teleport periods in the baseline window.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Only the `iscell` filter is applied (suite2p manual curation). The AI explicitly decides NOT to apply the putative interneuron filter (dF/F correlated with speed at r > 0.5). The iscell filter is applied AFTER computing dF/F (i.e., dF/F is computed for all ROIs, then subsetted).\n\nii.\n```python\niscell_full = ophys['ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/iscell'][:]\n...\ncell_mask_all.append(iscell_plane > 0)\n...\nevents, dff = compute_dff_and_deconvolve(F_concat, Fneu_concat, ...)  # all ROIs\ncell_indices = np.where(cell_mask)[0]\nevents_cells = events[cell_indices, :]  # filter after\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES state: \"We do NOT apply the interneuron correlation filter because: (a) it would require computing the full dF/F timeseries first and correlating with speed, (b) it only excludes ~0.42% of cells, (c) the iscell manual curation already removed obvious interneurons.\"\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Neural data is aligned to trial start. The trial boundaries (from `trial_start` to `teleport`) define the slice of neural data for each trial, so alignment is inherent in the slicing.\n\nii.\n```python\ns = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\ne = teleport_inds[i] - 1\ntrial_neural = events_cells[:, s:e].copy()\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify alignment to start of trial. No additional temporal shifting is needed.\n\n## 2-e. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. The data is kept at the original imaging frame rate (~15.5 Hz, ~64.5 ms per frame). No rebinning is applied. The time bin size is computed as `1000 / 15.5078125` ms.\n\nii.\n```python\n'time_bin_size': 1000.0 / 15.5078125,  # ms per frame\n```\n\niii. The CONVERSION_NOTES confirm \"Time bin = imaging frame: Each time bin is one imaging frame (~64.5 ms at 15.5 Hz).\"\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Time from start of trial in seconds* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the frame index within the trial and the effective imaging rate. NOT from the stored behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\ntime_from_start = np.arange(n_tp, dtype=np.float32) / effective_rate\n```\n\niii. The AI computes time from the frame count and frame rate rather than using stored timestamps. Since timestamps are evenly spaced at the imaging rate, this should give very similar results.\n\n## 3-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Time from start of trial in seconds*?\n\ni. A simple sequence of frame indices divided by the effective frame rate. The first timepoint is 0 seconds.\n\nii.\n```python\ntime_from_start = np.arange(n_tp, dtype=np.float32) / effective_rate\n```\n\niii. Straightforward computation.\n\n## 3-c. How is the `input` *Time from start of trial in seconds* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Both share the same frame indices (the trial slice from `s` to `e`), so they are inherently aligned. The number of timepoints in `time_from_start` equals `n_tp = e - s`, the same as the neural data slice.\n\nii.\n```python\nn_tp = e - s\ntrial_neural = events_cells[:, s:e].copy()\ntime_from_start = np.arange(n_tp, dtype=np.float32) / effective_rate\n```\n\niii. Neural and behavioral data use the same time indexing.\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Environment type* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `environment` behavior time series in the NWB file.\n\nii.\n```python\nenvironment = bts['environment/data'][:]\n...\nenv_per_trial = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\nfor i in range(n_trials):\n    s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n    e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n    env_vals = environment[s:e]\n    valid_env = env_vals[env_vals >= 0]\n    if len(valid_env) > 0:\n        env_per_trial[i] = int(np.median(valid_env))\n```\n\niii. Environment is constant within a trial (0 or 1), so taking the median of valid values gives the correct value.\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Environment type*?\n\ni. The median of valid (>= 0) environment values within each trial is taken. Invalid values (-1, which appear before scanning starts) are excluded. If no valid values exist, the previous trial's value is used.\n\nii.\n```python\nvalid_env = env_vals[env_vals >= 0]\nif len(valid_env) > 0:\n    env_per_trial[i] = int(np.median(valid_env))\nelif i > 0:\n    env_per_trial[i] = env_per_trial[i - 1]\n```\n\niii. Since environment is constant within a trial, the median is equivalent to just taking any valid sample.\n\n## 5-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Trial number* derived from?\n\ni. Trial number is the within-session trial index, derived from the loop counter over trials.\n\nii.\n```python\nfor i in range(n_trials):\n    ...\n    trial_number = np.float32(i)\n```\n\niii. The trial number is a sequential 0-indexed counter within the session.\n\n## 5-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Trial number*?\n\ni. No processing beyond assigning the loop index `i`. The value is broadcast to all timepoints within the trial.\n\nii.\n```python\ntrial_number = np.float32(i)\n...\nnp.full((1, n_tp), trial_number, dtype=np.float32)\n```\n\niii. Simple sequential indexing.\n\n## 6-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Previous trial outcome* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `Reward` timestamps and `autoreward` behavior time series. The AI pre-computes a per-trial `rewarded` array, and the previous trial's value becomes the input.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_timestamps = bts['Reward/timestamps'][:]\n...\nrewarded = determine_reward_per_trial(reward_timestamps, behav_timestamps, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds)\n# Also check autoreward\nfor i in range(n_trials):\n    s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n    e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n    if np.any(autoreward[s:e] > 0):\n        rewarded[i] = 1\n```\n\niii. The AI includes autoreward in the reward determination. The reference does not include autoreward.\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n\ni. For each trial, the previous trial's reward outcome (from the pre-computed `rewarded` array, which includes autoreward) is used. For the first trial, set to 0.\n\nii.\n```python\nif i == 0:\n    prev_outcome = np.float32(0)\nelse:\n    prev_outcome = np.float32(rewarded[i - 1])\n```\n\niii. Binary previous outcome (0=omitted, 1=rewarded).\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone is determined by examining where the `reward_zone` signal is nonzero and classifying by nearest zone center.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef determine_reward_zone_per_trial(position, rz_signal, trial_starts, teleports):\n    ...\n    rz_active = trial_rz > 0\n    if np.any(rz_active):\n        rz_positions = trial_pos[rz_active]\n        rz_center = np.mean(rz_positions)\n    ...\n    dists = {k: abs(rz_center - c) for k, c in ZONE_CENTERS.items()}\n    zone = min(dists, key=dists.get)\n```\n\niii. The AI uses a simple nearest-center approach. The reference uses a Viterbi algorithm for more stable assignments. The AI handles missing reward zone data by using the previous trial's zone.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. Signed distance from animal's position to the nearest edge of the assigned reward zone. Negative = before zone, 0 = in zone, positive = past zone. Then discretized into 7 bins.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position, zone_start, zone_end):\n    dist = np.zeros_like(position)\n    before = position < zone_start\n    inside = (position >= zone_start) & (position <= zone_end)\n    after = position > zone_end\n    dist[before] = position[before] - zone_start\n    dist[inside] = 0.0\n    dist[after] = position[after] - zone_end\n    return dist\n```\n\niii. Standard signed distance computation. Matches the reference logic.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Discretized into 7 bins using explicit boolean conditions:\n- 0: < -50 cm\n- 1: -50 to -10 cm\n- 2: -10 to 0 cm\n- 3: == 0 cm (in zone)\n- 4: >0 to 10 cm\n- 5: 10 to 50 cm\n- 6: > 50 cm\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_distance_to_rz(distance):\n    bins = np.zeros(len(distance), dtype=np.int64)\n    bins[distance < -50] = 0\n    bins[(distance >= -50) & (distance < -10)] = 1\n    bins[(distance >= -10) & (distance < 0)] = 2\n    bins[distance == 0] = 3\n    bins[(distance > 0) & (distance <= 10)] = 4\n    bins[(distance > 10) & (distance <= 50)] = 5\n    bins[distance > 50] = 6\n    return bins\n```\n\niii. The bins match the instructions. The reference uses `np.digitize` with a `1e-6` separator between \"0 cm\" and \">0 cm\" bins, while the AI uses explicit `== 0` and `> 0` conditions. Both correctly assign \"in zone\" to bin 3.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Position data and neural data share the same frame indices within each trial, so no additional alignment is needed.\n\nii.\n```python\ntrial_pos = position[s:e]\ntrial_neural = events_cells[:, s:e].copy()\n```\n\niii. Both use the same `s:e` slice.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Absolute position* derived from?\n\ni. Discretized into 5 equal-sized bins of 90 cm each spanning the 450 cm track.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_position(position):\n    bins = np.zeros(len(position), dtype=np.int64)\n    bins[position < 90] = 0\n    bins[(position >= 90) & (position < 180)] = 1\n    bins[(position >= 180) & (position < 270)] = 2\n    bins[(position >= 270) & (position < 360)] = 3\n    bins[position >= 360] = 4\n    return bins\n```\n\niii. Matches the instructions (5 bins, 90 cm each).\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *Absolute position* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Direct read from NWB lick data.\n\n## 9-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Lick*?\n\ni. Two-step processing: (1) Lick sensor error correction -- if more than 35% of frames in a trial have cumulative lick > 2, the entire trial's lick data is zeroed out. (2) Binarization -- any positive lick value mapped to 1.\n\nii.\n```python\nlick_corrected = lick.copy()\nfor i in range(n_trials):\n    s = trial_start_inds[i] - 1\n    e = teleport_inds[i] - 1\n    trial_lick = lick_corrected[s:e]\n    n_frames = len(trial_lick)\n    if n_frames > 0 and np.sum(trial_lick > 2) / n_frames > LICK_ERROR_THR:\n        lick_corrected[s:e] = 0\nlick_binary = (lick_corrected > 0).astype(np.int64)\n```\n\niii. The lick sensor error correction comes from the reference code (`correct_lick_sensor_error` in behavior.py). The threshold of 35% matches the paper. The reference solution does NOT apply this correction.\n\n## 9-c. How is `output` *Lick* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Same time indices as neural data.\n\nii. `trial_lick = lick_binary[s:e]`\n\niii. Same slice.\n\n## 10-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Reward zone location* derived from?\n\ni. Binary: 0=no, 1=yes.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef determine_reward_per_trial(reward_timestamps, behav_timestamps, trial_starts, teleports):\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_starts[i] - 1\n        e = teleports[i] - 1\n        t_start = behav_timestamps[s]\n        t_end = behav_timestamps[min(e, len(behav_timestamps) - 1)]\n        in_trial = (reward_timestamps >= t_start) & (reward_timestamps <= t_end)\n        if np.any(in_trial):\n            rewarded[i] = 1\n    return rewarded\n```\n\niii. The reference does not include autoreward in the reward outcome determination.\n\n## 12. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Several cases:\n- **Empty trials**: Trials where `e <= s` are skipped.\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active use the previous trial's zone (or default to A).\n- **NaN in neural data**: After deconvolution, NaN values are replaced with 0.\n- **Lick sensor errors**: Trials with >35% frames having lick > 2 have lick data zeroed.\n- **Trial count mismatch**: If trial_start and teleport counts differ, truncate to the shorter.\n- **Sessions with < 2 trials**: Skipped entirely.\n\nii.\n```python\ntrial_neural[np.isnan(trial_neural)] = 0\n...\nif e <= s:\n    continue\n...\nif len(neural_trials) < 2:\n    continue\n```\n\niii. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. The paper computes its own neural signal rather than using a stored one in `preprocessing.dff(F, Fneu, ..., deconvolve=True)` and stores the result as `sess.timeseries['events']`. How is the `neural` data processed? \n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n\nWhether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n\nThe neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n\n## 2-c. 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        if s < 0:\n            s = 0\n        if e > n_timepoints:\n            e = n_timepoints\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]\n        f_neu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n\n    # Step 2: Neuropil subtraction\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * f_neu_\n\n    # Step 3-4: Baseline computation and dF/F per trial\n    nanmask = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    flow = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n    dff = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n    spks = np.full_like(f_, np.nan)\n\n    for start, stop in zip(start_inds, stop_inds):\n        s = start - 1\n        e = stop - 1\n        if s < 0:\n            s = 0\n        if e > n_timepoints:\n            e = n_timepoints\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n\n        # Step 7: Deconvolve with OASIS\n        trial_dff = dff[:, s:e].copy()\n        trial_dff[np.isnan(trial_dff)] = 0\n        spks[:, s:e] = oasis(trial_dff, 2000, TAU, frame_rate / n_planes)\n\n    return spks, dff\n\n\ndef determine_reward_zone_per_trial(position, rz_signal, trial_starts, teleports):\n    \"\"\"\n    Determine reward zone label (A, B, C) for each trial based on\n    where the reward_zone signal is nonzero.\n\n    Returns:\n        zone_labels: list of str ('A', 'B', 'C') per trial\n        zone_coords: list of (start, end) tuples per trial\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(trial_starts)\n    zone_labels = []\n    zone_coords = []\n\n    for i in range(n_trials):\n        s = trial_starts[i] - {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '261,520p' /tests/reference_DECISIONS.md\"","aggregated_output":"```\n\niii. The trial number is simply the sequential index of the trial within the session.\n\n## 6-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Previous trial outcome* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `Reward` behavior time series. Reward event timestamps are matched to behavior timestamps, and a binary `isreward` array marks timepoints where rewards occurred.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_amounts = behavior_data['Reward'].data[:][:T]\nreward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:]\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n```\n\niii. The `Reward` time series has its own timestamps (not aligned to the behavior sampling rate), so `searchsorted` is used to find the nearest timepoint. An assertion checks that the alignment error is within half a time bin.\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Previous trial outcome*?\n\ni. For each trial, check whether any reward event occurred in the *previous* trial's time range. For the first trial, set to 0. The value is constant across all timepoints within a trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nif trial == 0:\n    input_curr[3,:] = 0\nelse:\n    prev_reward_idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial-1], trial_end_idx[trial-1], dtype=int)\n    isprevreward = np.any(isreward[prev_reward_idx])\n    input_curr[3,:] = int(isprevreward)\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify previous trial outcome as binary (omitted=0, rewarded=1). The code checks if any reward event fell within the previous trial's time boundaries.\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\n\n```\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. The bin edges match the instructions. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-d. No processing beyond extracting the per-trial slice and discretizing. Within the converted trials the position ranges from -0.8 to 451.8 cm, so the open first and last bins absorb the few samples that fall just outside the track (185 of 1,307,665). \n\nii.\n```python\nposition_curr = position[idx]\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\n```python\nposition_bins = [-np.inf,90,180,270,360,np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. The raw position values are used directly. Each lap starts at 0 cm and the track is 450 cm long (Methods), so five 90 cm bins over 0 to 450 are equal-sized by construction. The survey's wider -50 to 450 range comes from including the inter-trial teleport period, which is not part of any converted trial.\n\n## 8-c. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 90, 180, 270, 360, inf]`, corresponding to 90 cm wide bins spanning the 450 cm track. \n\nii.\n```python\nposition_bins = [-np.inf,90,180,270,360,np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. Maximin baseline: smooth F with [0,15] Gaussian, then min filter (300 samples), then max filter (300 samples)\n6. dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|\n7. Smooth dF/F with 2-sample Gaussian\n8. Deconvolve with OASIS: `dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau=0.7, frame_rate/n_planes)`\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n- 11 subjects: m3, m4, m7, m11, m12, 14 mice\" |\n| Neural data time bin | ~64.5 ms | ~15.5 Hz imaging rate |\n| Behavior data time bin | ~64.5 ms | Aligned to imaging frames |\n| Reward omission rate | ~15% | \"randomly omitted on ~15%
